children: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has received a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to introduce futures contracts on corporate bond indices, paving the way for a new exchange-traded instrument in India’s fixed-income derivatives market.
The approval follows a NOC from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for introducing the contracts under the prescribed regulatory framework.

Corporate bond index futures are expected to give market participants a standardised way to manage exposure to movements in corporate bond valuations, including those arising from changes in interest rates and credit spreads. The contracts are also expected to facilitate portfolio-level hedging and allow eligible market participants to take directional views on the corporate bond market.
The new product will add to the growing ecosystem of fixed-income exchange-traded products, including ETFs and other passive debt investment instruments.

Sriram Krishnan, Chief Business Development Officer at NSE, said India’s corporate bond market has “witnessed significant growth over the years”, creating opportunities for products aimed at the evolving needs of investors.

He said the introduction of corporate bond index futures would help bridge the gap between the growing underlying bond market and the availability of exchange-traded investment and risk-management instruments.
NSE said the contracts are expected to support greater transparency, wider market participation and improved efficiency in India’s corporate bond market.

The exchange will now undertake the operational preparations required for introducing the contracts under the applicable regulatory framework. Details of the contract specifications and commencement of trading will be announced separately.

title: NSE gets RBI nod to introduce corporate bond index futures
